domain_entities.name: LeaveRequest
domain_entities.purpose: Represents an employee's request for leave of a specific type across a date range. Tracks the full lifecycle from draft through submission, approval/rejection, and cancellation.
lifecycle_states: DRAFT — initial state; request is being prepared by the employee, not yet visible to managers
SUBMITTED — employee has submitted the request; visible to the assigned manager for action
APPROVED — manager has approved the request; leave balance is deducted; terminal state (unless cancelled)
REJECTED — manager has rejected the request; no balance impact; terminal state
CANCELLED — request was cancelled by the employee; if previously APPROVED, balance is restored; terminal state

domain_entities.name: LeaveRequestTransitions
domain_entities.purpose: Documents the valid state transitions for LeaveRequest and the guards/effects associated with each transition.
lifecycle_states: DRAFT → SUBMITTED (submit): employee finalizes and submits the request; requires startDate ≤ endDate, leaveTypeId references an active LeavePolicy, employee is ACTIVE
SUBMITTED → APPROVED (approve): manager approves; requires managerId matches the employee's managerId, balance check passes (remainingDays ≥ requested days), audit record written
SUBMITTED → REJECTED (reject): manager rejects; requires a rejectionReason; no balance impact; audit record written
DRAFT → CANCELLED (cancel): employee cancels their own draft; no balance impact
SUBMITTED → CANCELLED (cancel): employee cancels a submitted request; no balance impact
APPROVED → CANCELLED (cancel): employee cancels an approved request; balance is restored (usedDays decremented); audit record written

domain_entities.name: LeavePolicy
domain_entities.purpose: Defines the rules and entitlements for a specific leave type. Controls how many days employees are entitled to, whether manager approval is required, and any constraints like minimum notice periods.
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE — policy is in effect; employees can request leave under this policy
INACTIVE — policy is suspended; no new requests accepted; existing approved leave unaffected

domain_entities.name: Employee
domain_entities.purpose: Represents an employee in the organization. Tracks employment status which gates leave eligibility. Links to a manager for the approval chain.
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE — employee is currently employed and eligible for leave
INACTIVE — employee is on extended leave or suspension; leave requests are blocked
TERMINATED — employee is no longer with the organization; all leave access revoked

domain_entities.name: LeaveBalance
domain_entities.purpose: Tracks an employee's leave entitlement, usage, and remaining balance for a specific leave policy within a fiscal year. Deducted when leave is approved; restored when approved leave is cancelled.
lifecycle_states: OPEN — balance is active for the current fiscal year; accruals and deductions apply
CLOSED — balance has been finalized for a past fiscal year; read-only

domain_entities.name: LeaveType
attributes: ANNUAL — annual leave; typically planned in advance; requires manager approval
SICK — sick leave; may be taken on short notice; may require medical certificate after N consecutive days
EMERGENCY — emergency leave; urgent and unplanned; requires manager approval but may bypass minimum notice
domain_entities.purpose: Enumeration of leave categories. Each type maps to a LeavePolicy that defines the specific rules for that category.

business_rules: BR-001 — Employment eligibility: Only employees with employmentStatus = ACTIVE may submit a leave request. INACTIVE and TERMINATED employees are blocked.
domain_notes:
Lifecycle states introduced across entities:
- LeaveRequest: DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED
- LeavePolicy: ACTIVE, INACTIVE
- Employee: ACTIVE, INACTIVE, TERMINATED (employmentStatus)
- LeaveBalance: OPEN, CLOSED

These states must be reflected in the architectureMdUpdate so the chief architect can track them. The LeaveRequest has the richest lifecycle with 5 states and 6 named transitions (submit, approve, reject, cancel — with cancel having 3 source states). LeaveBalance is tightly coupled to LeaveRequest: APPROVED triggers deduction, CANCELLED (from APPROVED) triggers restoration. All state-changing operations require audit records per GP-002.
